sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Ficaria verna (synonym Ranunculus ficaria) is a small spring-flowering perennial geophyte, usually 10–30 cm tall. It grows in damp woods and cool, rich soils.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: Its glossy, heart-shaped leaves accompany starry yellow flowers about 2–3 cm across. Tubers form on the roots, and small bulbils may grow in leaf axils.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The fresh plant contains irritating, toxic protoanemonin, especially while flowering. Reports of eating leaves picked before flowering do not establish safety; do not consume it without reliable preparation guidance.
